# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** Two Ways: The Righteous and the Sinner

---

**3:1** Wake up, O my soul! Why do you sleep —
why do you not bless the LORD?

**3:2** Sing a new song to God, who is worthy of all praise;
sing out with joy, all you who love him!

**3:3** The LORD shapes the righteous through discipline;
the life of the righteous is forged in the instruction of the LORD.

**3:4** Our God is compassionate and merciful —
he forgives, he saves.

**3:5** The righteous man trips and the LORD sets him right;
he falls, and watches to see what God will do.

**3:6** He keeps looking for where help will come from,
his eyes are fixed on God alone.

**3:7** The righteous man spares himself nothing
when he makes atonement for some sin of ignorance;

**3:8** he scrubs his soul clean from defilement
and looks to God about the sin he did not know he had done —

**3:9** that it not be counted against him as a willful transgression,
that no enemy gets to trample him down.

**3:10** The sinner trips and curses his own life,
the day of his birth and the pain his mother endured for him.

**3:11** He piles sin on top of sin;
he falls — and what a final fall — and he will never rise again.

**3:12** The sinner's destruction is forever;
he will not be remembered when God comes to visit the righteous.
That is the fate of sinners — forever.
But those who fear the LORD shall rise to eternal life;
their life will be in the LORD's own light — and it will never end.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering prioritizing poetic force and contemporary resonance. Sense-for-sense.*
